summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: JPMorgan rounds up partners
articles.description: The biggest U.S. bank has been collecting payments partners to better integrate software and keep up with industry trends, among other purposes.

articles.title: Upgrade applies for ILC charter
articles.description: The decade-old credit-card startup named a SoFi alum and longtime regulator as CEO of its proposed bank.

articles.title: Visa moves ahead in China
articles.description: The card network giant said it won approval from the Chinese government to begin preparing to offer card services domestically in the country.

articles.title: Stablecoin startups advance payments
articles.description: Entrepreneurs embracing the digital assets are pushing payments modernization forward, and bringing incumbents along too.

articles.title: Fed names new payments chief
articles.description: Federal Reserve Financial Services tapped Kim Robbins to succeed Mark Gould starting in November.

articles.title: Visa-Mastercard payouts top $631M
articles.description: The tally of merchants receiving funds from a $5.5 billion settlement with the networks is nearing 700,000, according to a claims update.

articles.title: Where platforms are losing (and winning) merchants: Inside switching triggers
articles.description: Merchants are willing to switch. Learn which platform factors drive loyalty and retention.

articles.title: Block envisions bitcoin for all
articles.description: The company’s head of bitcoin, Miles Suter, has two big tasks: Make bitcoin a routine payment tool and change the global financial system.
